_note: Build Your Future. Triggers are implemented as typed predicates in src/lib/simulator.ts (keyed by rule id); the trigger strings here are documentation only. Credit assumptions come from HubSpot's credits documentation.

assumptions.tooltip: Assumes a 30-day month, the top-tier included allowance of 5,000 credits, and HubSpot Customer Agent at 50 credits per resolved conversation. Credit packs can be bought to keep agents running.

hubspot.text: A separate process per business line typically needs custom objects, which are top tier only.

salesforce.text: Record types give each line of business its own process, fields and layouts.

hubspot.text: A company can have one parent; activities and deals don't roll up to the parent.

salesforce.text: Multi-level account hierarchies roll up across every brand and location.

rules.short: Brands roll up to a parent

hubspot.text: Different access per brand or team needs field-level permissions, which are top tier only.

salesforce.text: Record-level security, sharing rules and role hierarchies across every business unit.

hubspot.text: Each HubSpot account is capped at 2,500 users.

salesforce.text: The same platform runs some of the world's largest enterprises.

hubspot.text: No native field service; dispatch needs a marketplace app.

salesforce.text: Field Service: scheduling, dispatch and a technician mobile app on the same platform.

hubspot.text: Customer Agent's voice channel is in beta.
Extra API capacity is sold as an add-on; ask whether two-way ERP sync is native or a custom build.

salesforce.text: MuleSoft and Informatica connect the ERP, billing and dispatch systems.

hubspot.text: Two-way data warehouse sync requires Data Hub.

salesforce.text: Data 360 Zero Copy reads warehouse data in place.

hubspot.text: Included credits cover about {daysCovered} days a month. After that, agents pause unless you buy credit packs.

salesforce.text: Flex Credits last the whole contract term, with no overage penalty.

emptyState: At this size, either works. Slide anything up and watch what changes.
honestyNote: This shows how capabilities and limits change as you grow, not prices. Salesforce adds licenses as you grow too, and every one lands on the same platform.
